summary: Okta group expiry policy blocks temporary access to Feature Flags console for contractors
description:
Issue summary: Several contractors reported immediate 403 / Access Denied when opening the Feature Flags console after receiving a temporary access approval. Impact: Contractors who were previously in ff-admin-like groups were removed by Okta due to an applied group expiry policy (Okta Lifecycle), causing RBAC lookups to deny access. This affects runbooks and time-sensitive release toggles.

Observed behavior: After approval flow completes, the user lands on the console sign-in but receives 403 and no RBAC roles are returned. Okta System Log shows a GroupMembership.deactivate event for the contractor groups around the same timestamp as the approval. SCIM provisioner logs show a subsequent "ignored" deprovision event attributable to an attribute mapping mismatch (expiredUntil != expirationDate).

Expected behavior: Temporary access approvals should result in users being in a valid group/role for the requested TTL and SCIM + RBAC should remain consistent for the life of that approval. Group expiry policy changes in Okta should not silently drop active temporary approvals without a re-provision attempt or alert.

Business impact: Blocks contractors from completing feature flag reviews and emergency toggles; could delay production fixes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision contractor user and add to 'contractor-ff-admins' with Okta expiry set to 7 days
2) Trigger self-service temporary approval (internal feature-flags console) and complete SSO sign-in
3) Observe immediate 403 on console even though approval flow completed
4) Check Okta System Log for GroupMembership.deactivate and SCIM provisioner logs for a rejected deprovision mapping
logs: Okta System Log: 2026-03-10T14:02:03Z GroupMembership.deactivate userId=00u9abcD reason=expiry policy
SCIM Provisioner: 2026-03-10T14:02:04Z WARN - incoming group change: user=evan.contributor@acme.com mapping mismatch: expiredUntil vs expirationDate -> action=ignored
RBAC Service: 2026-03-10T14:02:05Z INFO - lookup roles for userId=00u9abcD returned empty set (cache miss)
comments: Evan Morales (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Customer-facing contractor reported 403 after approval completed; raising as P1 since it blocks releases.
Oncall (SRE) 2026-03-10: Initial triage - looks like Okta group expiry events are arriving during approval flow. Suspect lifecycle policy change push last night.
Priya Nair (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Assigned. Reproduced locally with test contractor account. Will instrument SCIM mapping and propose workaround.

Identity Eng (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-11: Confirmed Okta org has a new Group Expiry Rule applied to groups with name pattern 'contractor-*' rolled out 2026-03-09. SCIM mapping expects 'expirationDate' while Okta uses 'expiredUntil' TTL attribute in this rule.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 14:30 UTC - Reproduced with test account; auth flow completes but RBAC returns empty due to missing group membership row.
2026-03-10 15:10 UTC - Reviewed Okta System Logs: batch of GroupMembership.deactivate events coincide with approval timestamps. No explicit re-provision attempt observed.

2026-03-10 16:00 UTC - SCIM Provisioner (provisioner-3) code path ignores group change when attribute key != configured mapping; attribute key mismatch 'expiredUntil' vs 'expirationDate' prevents deactivation handling path from reconciling state.
2026-03-11 09:00 UTC - Session behavior: existing active sessions continue until cookie expiry; new logins fail because group membership already removed in Okta and not present in RBAC DB.

Hypothesis: Recent Okta Lifecycle rule introduced a TTL attribute key name incompatible with our SCIM mapping. SCIM treats deprovision events as 'ignored', leaving RBAC in inconsistent state (no re-add).
resolution:
Workaround applied 2026-03-11: Identity Eng rolled back the Okta Group Expiry Rule for 'contractor-*' groups to prevent further deactivations. Manually reconciled 14 affected contractor accounts by re-provisioning group memberships and running the RBAC sync job.

Permanent fix: Update SCIM provisioner mapping to accept both 'expiredUntil' and 'expirationDate' attributes, and add an alert rule for sudden group membership delta (>5% change in 5 minutes) for monitored groups. Created follow-up INT task to ship the mapping change and tests.

Follow-ups: identity team to schedule a postmortem and update the approval flow to validate group membership post-Okta events before presenting final success to the user.
